Criterion: Verify that adequate engine bay/nacelle cooling and ventilation provisions exist. Standard: Engine bay/nacelle cooling and ventilation provisions are adequate to maintain the temperatures of power plant components, engine fluids, other bay/nacelle equipment and structure within the temperature limits established for these components and fluids, under ground and flight operating conditions, and after normal engine shutdown. Refer to 8.4 for further fire protection provisions. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, simulation, inspection and review of documentation. Temperature limit requirements are verified by inspection of design documentation. System thermal performance is verified by inspection of design analysis, thermal models and simulations. Engine bay/nacelle environments are verified by thermal surveys during ground and flight tests. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.7.10, A.4.7.10 engine exhaust nozzle system design and verification.

versions.text:
Standard: Engine bay or nacelle cooling, and ventilation maintain the temperatures of engine components, structures, engine fluids, and bay or nacelle equipment within the temperature limits established for these components and fluids when operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1 for the stated life documented in engine technical data. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review design documentation to verify temperature limits are defined for engine components, structures, engine fluids, and bay or nacelle equipment. Analysis.
  (1) Thermal analysis and modeling of engine components, engine fluids, and bay or nacelle equipment verifies system thermal performance and that no temperature limits are exceeded. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Installed engine ground testing verifies engine bay or nacelle cooling, and ventilation. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Flight testing verifies engine bay or nacelle cooling, and ventilation.
